definition: The process of splitting long documents or text into smaller segments for processing, indexing, or inclusion in a model's context.
details: Chunking strategy (size, overlap, and boundaries) significantly affects retrieval quality in RAG systems, since chunks that are too large may dilute relevance while chunks that are too small may lose important context.
story: Picture an engineer at a cluttered workbench, turning a clever idea over in their hands until it finally clicks. Boil it down and it is this: The process of splitting long documents or text into smaller segments for processing, indexing, or inclusion in a model's context. Here is why it matters: Chunking strategy (size, overlap, and boundaries) significantly affects retrieval quality in RAG systems, since chunks that are too large may dilute relevance while chunks that are too small may lose important context. It is one of those ideas that feels obvious only after someone shows it to you. And that idea, made concrete, is Chunking.
